description: Generalise the Darwin-only PS1 iOS path in scripts/build-core.sh into a reusable iOS builder that covers all five cores (fceumm, mgba, genesis_plus_gx, snes9x, pcsx_rearmed), behind a NEW subcommand namespace so the WASM web build is untouched. `scripts/build-core.sh ios <core>` builds one core as an aarch64-apple-ios .dylib into native/ios/build/lib/; `ios-all` builds all five; `ios-names` prints the five canonical dylib filenames and is the only iOS subcommand that runs on a non-Darwin host, which makes the filename table testable in the Linux sandbox. Bare `build-core.sh fceumm|mgba|genesis_plus_gx|snes9x|all` keeps meaning WASM exactly as today, and `build-core.sh pcsx_rearmed` stays working as a backwards-compatible alias for `ios pcsx_rearmed`.
steps: Rewrite the script header comment so the two namespaces are unmistakable: the existing WASM usage lines stay exactly as they are, and a second block documents `ios <core>`, `ios-all` and `ios-names`. Say in the header WHY the split exists: `build-core.sh fceumm` is a live, documented WASM invocation (web/cores/README.md, README.md, SESSION_HANDOFF.md, scripts/core-abi-test.mjs buildHint strings, .github/workflows/deploy.yml), so overloading a core name to mean iOS would break the web build.

Replace the single-core PS1 section with an `iOS native cores` section holding the canonical table. Define IOS_CORES=(fceumm mgba genesis_plus_gx snes9x pcsx_rearmed) and IOS_OUT_DIR=native/ios/build/lib once, and an ios_core_config() case block that sets, per core, the repo URL, the canonical dylib filename, the build kind (make or cmake), the makefile name, the subdirectory make must run in, whether submodules are needed and a human display name. Every canonical filename is written exactly once, in that case block, with a comment listing the five downstream files that must agree with it.

Add ios_require_darwin(), which keeps the existing clear non-macOS error (generalised past PS1) and the xcrun/make/git tool checks, and ios_resolve_sdk(), which resolves the iphoneos SDK path once with `xcrun --sdk iphoneos --show-sdk-path` and fails if it is empty or not a directory.

Add ios_clone(), cloning into .work/ios/<core> rather than .work/<core>. This is deliberate: the WASM path clones the same repositories into .work/<core> and both builds compile IN TREE, so sharing a directory would let stale wasm objects be linked into an iOS dylib. Comment that reason. Clone shallow except for pcsx_rearmed, which needs full history for its recursive submodules (lightrec, libchdr).

Add ios_stage_dylib(), the one place that reasserts `install_name_tool -id @rpath/<canonical>` when otool -D disagrees, copies the artefact into native/ios/build/lib/<canonical>, and prints the staged path and size. The @rpath install name is what makes the runtime dlopen from Frameworks/ resolve through LD_RUNPATH_SEARCH_PATHS.

Add build_ios_make_core(): run `make -f <makefile> platform=ios-arm64 IOSSDK=<sdk> -j<ncpu>` in the core's make directory, then locate the produced dylib. Look for the canonical name first, fall back to any *.dylib in the make directory (a core may name its TARGET differently), and error clearly naming the core if nothing was produced. snes9x is covered by the make directory being `libretro` because its makefile sets CORE_DIR := ..; fceumm, genesis_plus_gx and pcsx_rearmed build at the repo root with Makefile.libretro.

Add build_ios_cmake_core() for mgba, which ships no makefile at all. Configure with CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=iOS, CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64, CMAKE_OSX_SYSROOT=<iphoneos sdk>, CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=16.0, BUILD_LIBRETRO=ON, LIBRETRO_STATIC=ON, SKIP_LIBRARY=ON and the same everything-off feature flags the WASM path already passes, build the mgba_libretro target to get mgba_libretro.a, then link the dylib with `cc -arch arm64 -isysroot <sdk> -miphoneos-version-min=16.0 -dynamiclib -install_name @rpath/mgba_libretro_ios.dylib -Wl,-force_load <archive> -framework Foundation -lm`. Comment that -force_load is load-bearing (nothing in the link references retro_*, so a plain archive link would produce an empty dylib), that -framework Foundation matches the OS_LIB mgba's CMakeLists appends on Apple, and that mgba's CMakeLists forces CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET to 10.6 inside its if(APPLE) block, which only lowers the objects' minimum OS.

Add build_ios_core() dispatching on the configured build kind, and build_all_ios_cores() which builds each core in a subshell so one failure cannot abort the rest, records pass/fail per core, prints a summary naming every failure, and exits non-zero if any core failed. Building all five in one run and reporting every failure at once matters because the macOS runner is the only compiler this project has.

Add the early dispatch, ABOVE ensure_toolchain and above the WASM `all` handling, for: `ios <core>`, `ios-all`, `ios-names`, and the `pcsx_rearmed` backwards-compatible alias. `ios` with no core, or with an unknown core, must print the list of valid iOS core names and exit 1. Nothing in this dispatch may call ensure_toolchain, so wasi-sdk is never fetched and web/cores/ is never created or written.

Leave the WASM machinery byte-identical below the dispatch: core_config, ensure_toolchain, clone_core, build_sources_strategy, build_cmake_strategy, build_core, RETRO_EXPORTS, the import-restriction check and the closing manifest reminder.
acceptance_criteria: `scripts/build-core.sh fceumm`, `mgba`, `genesis_plus_gx`, `snes9x` and `all` still reach the wasi-sdk WASM path and still write only to web/cores/; no core name means iOS.
`scripts/build-core.sh ios <core>` builds exactly one iOS dylib and `ios-all` builds all five; both refuse a non-Darwin host with a clear message naming what they would have needed.
`scripts/build-core.sh ios-names` prints exactly the five canonical filenames, one per line, on any host, without fetching wasi-sdk or touching web/.

The five canonical dylib filenames (fceumm_libretro_ios.dylib, mgba_libretro_ios.dylib, genesis_plus_gx_libretro_ios.dylib, snes9x_libretro_ios.dylib, pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib) are each written exactly once in this script and staged into native/ios/build/lib/.
Every staged dylib has its install name reasserted to @rpath/<canonical> when it differs.
A single core failing under `ios-all` names that core and the reason, does not stop the other four, and still makes the command exit non-zero.
The pcsx_rearmed build keeps its recursive submodule init and its platform=ios-arm64 invocation, so the working PS1 path does not regress.
iOS sources are cloned into .work/ios/<core>, separate from the WASM clones in .work/<core>.
bash -n scripts/build-core.sh is valid, and no em dashes were added.
verification: bash scripts/build-core.sh ios-names -> the five canonical filenames, and web/cores/ is not created or modified.
bash scripts/build-core.sh ios fceumm on this Linux host -> the Darwin guard message, exit 1, and no wasi-sdk download.
grep the script to confirm each canonical filename appears exactly once and that the early dispatch sits above ensure_toolchain.

By eye against the upstream makefiles read during planning: fceumm and genesis_plus_gx build at the root with Makefile.libretro, snes9x builds inside libretro/ because CORE_DIR := .., pcsx_rearmed keeps its submodules, and mgba is the CMake plus manual -force_load link.
The real macOS builds cannot run here and are verified only by the orchestrator's CI run.
findings: scripts/build-core.sh grew an iOS section that replaces the single-core PS1 path. New: IOS_CORES (fceumm mgba genesis_plus_gx snes9x pcsx_rearmed), IOS_OUT_DIR, IOS_WORK=.work/ios, IOS_MIN_VERSION=16.0, IOS_LEGACY_ALIAS, IOS_SELF, ios_core_config() as the ONE definition of the five canonical filenames, ios_print_names, ios_require_darwin, ios_resolve_sdk, ios_jobs, ios_clone, ios_stage_dylib, build_ios_make_core, build_ios_cmake_core, build_ios_core and build_all_ios_cores, plus a dispatch case above ensure_toolchain for ios / ios-all / ios-names and the pcsx_rearmed alias. The WASM machinery below the dispatch is byte-identical. Upstream facts were read from each core's own makefile rather than assumed: fceumm and Genesis-Plus-GX build at the repo root with Makefile.libretro, snes9x builds INSIDE libretro/ because its makefile sets CORE_DIR := .., pcsx_rearmed keeps its recursive submodules, and mgba ships no makefile at all so it is a CMake static-archive build plus a hand-written `cc -dynamiclib -Wl,-force_load ... -framework Foundation -lm` link. Three hardening changes came out of the semantic review and are worth naming: ios-all runs each core as a separate `bash` PROCESS rather than a subshell, because bash disables errexit inside a command used as an `if` condition and that suppression is inherited by subshells, which would have let a failed make fall through to the artefact check and report a stale dylib as ok (proved empirically in this sandbox, then fixed); the expected dylib is deleted before each build and before each staging so the persistent .work/ios tree cannot contribute a previous run's output; and ios_stage_dylib now asserts `nm -gU | grep -q retro_run`, which is the only check anywhere that would catch the empty dylib that a -force_load link over an LTO archive can produce. The make fallback search was also narrowed from *.dylib to *_libretro_ios.dylib, and the mgba configure now passes -DCMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_TARGET_TYPE=STATIC_LIBRARY pre-emptively rather than documenting it as the thing to try after a failed CI run. VERIFIED: bash -n clean; `ios-names` prints exactly the five names on Linux; `ios <core>`, `ios-all` and the pcsx_rearmed alias all hit the Darwin guard with exit 1; `ios` with no core and `ios bogus` both print the valid list; a stubbed-copy harness proves fceumm, mgba, genesis_plus_gx, snes9x, all and no-args still reach ensure_toolchain and build_core (the WASM path); each canonical filename appears exactly once in the script. The actual macOS core builds cannot run here and are proven only by the orchestrator's CI run.
